description: Common mutation operators, the ranking kind each one has, and how each engine's operator names map onto them. kind_factor is the 'mutant kind' factor of the survivor ranking (RUBRIC.md).

branch.meaning: changes a branch or boundary: comparison, negation, condition, logical operator, loop control

value.meaning: changes a computed value, a returned value, an argument, or removes a call

display.meaning: changes a string literal that is not compared and not a named constant (usually text shown or logged)

logical.example: a and b -> a or b

method_swap_logic.example: xs.some(p) -> xs.every(p); s.startsWith(a) -> s.endsWith(a); Math.min -> Math.max
method_swap_logic.note: Stryker's MethodExpression when it swaps a quantifier or a side: 'any holds' becomes 'all hold', which decides a branch

remove_method_call.example: name.upper() == ADMIN -> name == ADMIN; s.strip() -> s
remove_method_call.note: survives when no test uses an input whose case or whitespace differs

constant_string_compared.note: a string that is an operand of a comparison (==, !=, in, a literal tuple compared with in) decides a branch, like the comparison itself

constant_string_named.note: an UPPER_CASE module or class constant: usually a key, role or code that logic compares against, not display text

constant_string.note: builtin mutants inside a typing Literal[...] carry a note: they change behaviour only where the type is checked at run time (pydantic, typeguard), so judge them by whether such a check is in reach of the tests

builtin.note: builtin_mutator.py emits the common names directly, for Python (ast) and Go (go_mutator.py, Go tokens: comparison, logical, arithmetic, ++/--, break/continue, true/false, return err -> nil, if negation).

gremlins.note: gremlins (Go) has no mutation-testing-elements reporter of its own; a converted report keeps gremlins' mutator type in mutatorName, mapped here (over Stryker's names). INVERT_LOOPCTRL swaps break and continue, which changes which iterations run: a branch.

go-mutesting.note: go-mutesting (Go) names its mutators by path; a converted report keeps that name in mutatorName.

pit.note: PIT writes mutation-testing-elements through its report plugin; its mutator names are in the Stryker table below (ConditionalsBoundaryMutator, ...).

mutmut.note: mutmut 3 does not name its operators; normalize_results.py infers the common operator from each mutant's diff by comparing tokens.

stryker.note: Stryker (JS/TS, .NET, Scala) and PIT write the mutation-testing-elements JSON report; mutatorName is mapped here. EqualityOperator is refined from the replacement text (== / != is a negation, < / <= a boundary). MethodExpression is refined from the method names: some/every, startsWith/endsWith and min/max swaps are method_swap_logic, a dropped call (filter, sort, trim, slice) is remove_method_call, anything else stays call_args. The engine's own mutator name is kept in each mutant's engine_operator.
